package_info.why_malicious: No specific malicious package is described in this report. The article discusses broad trends and risks in software supply chain security, including the threat of malicious code being inserted into trusted software via supply chain attacks, but does not provide details of any particular malicious package or code sample.

behavioral_signatures: Insertion of malicious code into trusted software supply chain components
Unexpected network communications from build or CI/CD environments
Tampering with open-source dependencies or build scripts
file_indicators: Unexpected changes to package manifests (e.g., package.json, setup.py)
Presence of unauthorized scripts in build or deployment pipelines
Unusual or new files in open-source project repositories
network_indicators: Outbound connections to unknown or suspicious domains from build environments
Exfiltration of environment variables or secrets during build or install processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized changes to software supply chain components, such as dependency files and build scripts. Implement behavioral monitoring for unexpected network activity during build, install, or CI/CD pipeline execution. Use tools like SBOMs and security scorecards to assess the integrity and security posture of open-source dependencies. Watch for the presence of unauthorized scripts or files in repositories and deployment artifacts.
